title: Head Rush
footer: Sources: StatPearls, Orthostatic Hypotension · NHS, Low blood pressure

scenes.label: Seeing stars?
scenes.tts: Ever stood up too fast and saw stars? Here's what's happening inside you.
scenes.say: Ever stood up too fast and saw stars? Here's what's happening inside you.

scenes.label: ~0.5 L
scenes.sub: of blood drops toward your legs
scenes.tts: The second you stand, gravity pulls around half a litre of blood down into your legs and belly.
scenes.say: The second you stand, gravity pulls around half a litre of blood down into your legs and belly.

scenes.tts: So for a moment, your blood pressure dips and less blood reaches your brain. That's the dizzy, dark-vision feeling.
scenes.say: So for a moment, your blood pressure dips and less blood reaches your brain. That's the dizzy, dark-vision feeling.

scenes.label: ~15 sec
scenes.tts: Normally your body fixes it fast. Your heart speeds up, your blood vessels tighten, and your calf muscles squeeze blood back up. Usually within about fifteen seconds.
scenes.say: Normally your body fixes it fast. Your heart speeds up, your blood vessels tighten, and your calf muscles squeeze blood back up. Usually within about 15 seconds.

scenes.sub: pump your ankles first · take it slow in the morning
scenes.tts: To avoid it, get up in stages, and pump your ankles a few times before you stand. Take extra care first thing in the morning.
scenes.say: To avoid it, get up in stages, and pump your ankles a few times before you stand. Take extra care first thing in the morning.

scenes.sub: if it keeps happening or you faint, see a doctor
scenes.tts: Does this happen to you? Never, sometimes, or often? Tell me in the comments. And if it keeps happening, or you faint, see a doctor.
scenes.say: Does this happen to you? NEVER, SOMETIMES or OFTEN? Tell me in the comments. And if it keeps happening, or you faint, see a doctor.
